Nuair a tha Bing a’ cluich geama le fòn-làimhe Flop, chaneil rudan a’ dol mar bu chòir oir tha am fòn-làimhe a' briseadh nuair a tha e dol na sgeing air an làr. An àite seo innse do Flop, tha Bing ga chuir dhan bhiona. Tha e faireachdainn cho dona mun seo ach tha e ag ionnsachadh gum feum e innse mar a thachair.
When Bing is playing a game with Flop’s mobile phone, he accidentally drops the mobile and it breaks. Instead of telling Flop, he throws it in the bin. He feels upset about it all and learns that it’s best to tell the truth. Bing - Benny Walsh Flop - Iain Mackinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Mairi Morrison.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Bing aig cuirm sa phàirc, tha còir aige 'n oidhch' a chrìochnachadh ach tha e air bhioran agus tha e fàs cho diùid. Ge-tà, le taic bho charaidean, tha e faighinn seachad air na duilgheadasan sin agus tha e a' seinn Òran a’ Bhogha-fhroise.
When Bing is at a show in the park, he is extremely nervous as he is meant to be singing the finale. However, with help from his friends, Bing gets over all his insecurities and sings the Rainbow Song. Bing - Benny Walsh Flop - Iain Mackinnon Sula - Holly Duffy Amma - Evelyn Coull MacLeod Pando - Finlay Morrison Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Mairi Morrison.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:
Tha Ben a' leughadh sgeulachd dha na h-Abadas mus tig iad dhan leabaidh. Aig deireadh na sgeòil, tha iad airson an geama fhaclan a chlcuich, 's tha Hari ga fhaighinn fhèin sa ghàrradh a' coimhead son cailleach-oidhche.
Before going to bed, Ben reads Seren, Hari and Ela a story. When the story ends, the Abadas decide to play the word game and this sends Hari to a windy garden looking for an owl.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.sub-title: A’ Lorg nam Boga-bogadach/The Poc-Poc Hunt ║ CleasanAtaidh&Tilidh/TheAdventures/Abney&TealS1E10/52
programme.desc:
‘S e latha socair a th’ ann air an eilean, latha math airson a bhith dìomhain. Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ crochadh hamag, is tha tòrr spòrs aca a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre. Tha na Boga-bogadaich a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre cuideachd, ach tha iad air an caith suas dhan adhar is a’ dol a-mach à sealladh. Càite an deach iad? Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ falbh a’ lorg nam Boga-bogadach.
It is a lazy day on the Island. Abney, Teal and Neep put up a hammock and have a great time trying to get into it. The Poc-Pocs join in the fun but are thrown up into the air and disappear. Where have they gone? Abney, Teal and Neep go on a Poc-Poc hunt. Teal - Linda MacLeod Abney - Tony Kearney Producer - Linda MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Editor - Chas Chalmers Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc:
Ged a tha riochd caran neo-àbhaisteach air a’ Bhagan-mhara, tha e den bheachd gu bheil cuid eile ann an tha nas grainnde buileach na iad.
Although the Blobfish looks rather unusual, he says that there are other fish who are even more aesthetically displeasing than him. Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc:
Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Emily agus na coineanaich aice, Syrius agus Seumas a tha beothail agus bòidheach. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coineanaich agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios iad a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean.
Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home.
In this episode, Eilidh visits Emily and her adorable rabbits, Syrius and Seumas. We find out how to look after rabbits and about all the lovely stuff Emily, Syrius and Seumas get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home; including how best to handle, train and feed them. Presenter - Eilidh Cormack Producer - Donna Murchison Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc:
Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Dòmhnall Ruadh a’ leughadh An Ròn Beag. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Janis Mackay agus a dhealbhachadh le Gabby Grant. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill.
A bedtime story for young children. Donald Smith reads An Ròn Beag by Janis Mackay, illustrated by Gabby Grant and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald. Presenter - Donald Smith.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Gealach na Durraige Guirme a' nochdadh, tha i a’ taladh dhurragan gorma a tha glè thearc, ach blasta, agus ma dh'itheas Gumbal tè dhiubh, tha a h-uile càil a' dol ceàrr!
When the Blue Grub Moon appears, it brings out a very rare but delicious grub and if a Gumbal eats one, things go wrong! Troig/Rìgh - Iain Macrae Bonns/Merri - Mischa Macpherson Seonaidh - Lana Beaton Dùd/Snorg - Derek MacIntosh Glob - Calum MacKinnon Chank - Ruaraidh Munro Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Producer - Mairi Macleod.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc:

Bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean làitheil agus, mar thè a dh’ionnsaich na Gàidhlig i fhèin, bheir Joy mìneachadh dhuinn air briathrachas, gràmar is gnathasan-cainnte ann an dòigh a tha furasta a thuigsinn.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh a th’ air Gàidhlig ionnsachadh gu àrd ìre neo a thogadh leis a’ Ghàidhlig air falbh bho sgìrean traidiseanta na Gàidhealtachd, agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh dhuinn air annasan is cuspairean ’s e air chuairt air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot, ann am pod-chraolaidhean SpeakGaelic air BBC Sounds agus tha na prògraman air fad rin lorg le fo-thiotalan air sianal YouTube SpeakGaelic.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to keep on speaking Gaelic. As in previous series, she introduces and explain usage for words and phrases on everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through vocabulary, grammar and idiom on topics such as medicine, politics, community and exercise.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, and the intrepid Calum Maclean ventures to forgotten corners of Scotland seeking hidden treasures.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc:
Gregor MacLeod inherited his grannie’s old cookery book. In it she had written down over 50 recipes by hand and Gregor has set himself the challenge of cooking his way through them.
He takes on the classics shortbread and marmalade. Grannie has five recipes for shortbread alone but Gregor has to pick one. And the instructions for marmalade are sparing, so in search of advice he visits his neighbour, a prize-winning marmalade maker.
A real challenge is grannie’s recipe for oxtail stew. He visits another neighbour, a crofter, who happens to have one in the freezer and finds out more about this cut of meat and how to cook it. And guess who is coming to tea to taste the finished stew?
For pudding, grannie’s recipe for Bakewell tart is on the menu but this time with Gregor’s 21st century twist using the marmalade he made before.
Fhuair Griogar MacLeòid seann leabhar còcaireachd a sheanmhair mar dhìleab: comhairle na làmh-sgrìobhaidh fhèin air còrr is lethcheud dinnear is greim blasta a dhèanamh. Tha Griogar a’ cur roimhe a’ dol tron a leabhar a’ feuchainn orra.
Sa phrògram seo tha e a’ cumail ri biadh as aithne dhuinn uile, aran goirid agus marmailead. Bha còig dòighean aig granaidh ar aran-goirid a dhèanamh ach feumaidh Griogar aon a thaghadh. Chan eil cus comhairle aice dha mun mharmailead, is tha sin ga chur a shireadh beachd air nàbaidh, a ghlèidh duaisean air a shon.
Fìor annas do Ghriogar, se na bh’ aice ri ràdh mu earball mairt a bhruich. Ach tha nàbaidh eile le fear reòdhta a-staigh, agus gheibh Griogar barrachd comhairle air dè nì e leis. Agus saoil cò thig ga fheuchainn nuair a bhios e bruich?Airson mìlsean, tha tort Bakewell gu bhi aige agus cuiridh e a dhreach fhèin air le marmailead na luib.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Gregor Macleod Director - Ramsay MacMahon.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Air a togail san dàrna linn deug ann am meadhan Paris (air an Île de la Cité), aig aon àm b' e Notre-Dame a' chathair-eaglais a b' àirde air thalamh. Tha an t-soitheach aibhseach cloiche seo a' riochdachadh ailtireachd Gotach. Ach tha a seasmhachd a-nise ann an cunnart.
Rinn an teine milleadh air cothromachd an togalaich. Chaidh am mullach a sgrios, còmhla ris a' chliath iongantaich fiodha seo – air a dèanamh de mhìle craobh daraich – 's chaidh a losgadh san teine. Ach fhathast cha do thuit Notre-Dame. Dè as coireach gu bheil i cho làidir? Am measg an sprùillich chaidh iomadh ceangal meatailt a lorg, cuid de mheud iongantach. An robh iad nam pàirt dhen chiad dhealbhadh no nach robh? An gabhadh e a bhith gun do dh'fhuiling Notre-Dame trioblaidean structarail eile tro na linntean?
Leanaidh sinn gu dlùth an luchd-saidheans is na h-ailtirean is iad a' sgrùdadh a' chliath iongantach fiodha is meatailt a bh' air cùl na cloiche. Le cuideachadh bho dhealbhan 3D agus ath-achdachaidhean gheibh sinn tuigse air toiseach an togalaich mhòrail seo.
Built in the 12th century in the centre of Paris (on Île de la Cité), Notre-Dame was once the world's highest cathedral. This gigantic stone structure is the very essence of Gothic architecture. But today, its stability is compromised.
The 2019 fire greatly damaged the building's structure. Its roof was completely destroyed, as well as its incredible wooden frame, made of a thousand oaks, which was swallowed by the flames. Still, Notre-Dame did not collapse. What are the secrets of this exceptional strength? Amongst the wreckage, many metal fasteners were found, some of incredible size. Were they part of the original design or not? Is it possible that Notre-Dame encountered other structural problems throughout the centuries?
We closely follow scientists and architects as they study the impressive skeleton of wood and metal which hid behind the stone. Supported by 3D animations as well as re-enactments, their interventions allow us to grasp the genesis of this monumental structure.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Anna Murray Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Executive Producer - Shona Henderson Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.title: Sailm nan Daoine
programme.desc:
Tha Rob MacNeacail air turas gus sailm Ghàidhlig a sheinn is a sgaoileadh. ’S e film tarraingeach is togarrach a tha seo mu chumhachd na coimhearsnachd, an teaghlaich is an seasmhachd a tha a dhìth gus cànan a chumail beò.
Thòisich Rob air na sailm a ghabhail ann an Carlops gus comharrachadh ceann-bliadhna bàs athar, am bàrd Aonghas MacNeacail. Ged a tha na seiseanan a’ còrdadh ri muinntir a’ bhaile, tha Rob ga cheasnachadh fhèin a bheil còir aige a bhith a’ teagasg nan salm. Cha do dh’ionnsaich e mar a stiùireas e an t-seinn ach o chionn ghoirid, agus cha deach a thogail san eaglais. Chan eil Rob aig tàmh is e a’ faireachdainn gum feum e falbh air turas gus cluinntinn mar a bhios na Gàidheil a’ seinn nan salm anns na coimhearsnachdan a tha a’ cumail an traidisein beò.
Bheir an turas e bho na h-Eileanan an Iar gu Corcaigh an Iar, a’ leantainn seann shlighean a bheireas ceòl is beachdan ùra gu bith.
Rob MacNeacail embarks on a mission to sing Gaelic psalms. An entertaining and heartwarming film about the power of community, family and the resilience needed to keep a language alive.
Rob started singing the psalms in his home village of Carlops to mark the anniversary of the death of his father, the poet Aonghas MacNeacail. Although the sessions are popular with locals, Rob starts to question his authority to teach the psalms, as he only learned how to precent relatively recently and didn’t grow up in the church.
As spring turns to summer, Rob starts to feel restless and decides to hit the road to reconnect with his Gaelic roots and hear how psalms are sung by Gaels in the communities that nurture the tradition. His journey takes him from the Western Isles to West Cork in Ireland, following well-trodden ancient paths that unravel threads of music and ideas along the way.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Director - Jack Archer Executive Producer - John Archer Editor - James Alcock Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Production Manager - Mhairi Valentine Production Company - Hopscotch Films.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
While the teams get into the rhythm of their shopping, host Danny Sebastian indulges one of his passions at an exhibition in London. The Music Is Black: A British Story celebrates 125 years of the influence of black music on culture and communities. At the V&A East Museum, Danny tours the exhibition with curator Jacqueline Springer, looking at a vinyl record with the words ‘Race Records’ on the sleeve, a label designed to segregate black music from white artists. There’s a piano belonging to the first black artist to have a UK number one single, Winifred Attwell, engraved with the names of her fans, a dress worn by Dame Shirley Bassey at the 2013 Academy Awards and a Banksy-designed vest worn by Stormzy at Glastonbury in 2019.
Hoping to turn their items into auction hits are dad and daughter Erike and Melissa, and mum and daughter Angela and Katie. With hundreds of stalls to choose from, the teams go in search of profitable antiques with their experts, Irita Marriott and Jonathan Pratt.
While the red team sizes up a vintage measuring tape, the blues check out a crackle-glazed pig sculpture. Then it’s off to auction in Bourne End, Buckinghamshire, to try to sell their buys to the highest bidders. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
Ex-con Joe Ruby is a volunteer at a local priory, tending to the grounds, seeking forgiveness and attempting to start a new life, all under the kind but watchful eye of Father David.
But when the body of one of the monks is found hastily buried in a remote part of the priory grounds, Oxford-educated DI Rose O’Connell and her green second in command, DS Raj Singh, are sent to investigate.
The mysterious circumstances make it a tricky case to solve. What secrets are these sacred grounds hiding? And what do these God-fearing suspects know about the murder? There’s Brother Christopher, the gentle monk who loves to garden, Sister Marie, the stern but kindly nun who runs Bible class and Father David, the cryptic, ever-wise prior. Alongside them is the victim’s brother Benedict, who is someone in need of support and money. And then there’s Joe himself, who with his criminal past becomes suspect number one for Rose and Raj.
But when Joe comes up with some insights from his own dodgy history, Rose senses that he may prove useful after all.
Finding themselves investigating alongside each other, Joe and Rose set out to solve the mystery of who killed Brother Mark, frustrating each other at every turn, only to uncover a truth far more shocking than either anticipated. Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities.
One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies.
They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
As part of the BBC’s Music Is Black season, renowned choir director Mark De-Lisser visits the new exhibition of the same name at the V&A East Museum and introduces exhilarating new music from the London Community Gospel Choir and special guests.
Mark takes a guided tour with curator Jacqueline Springer to explore how black music and the sounds and songs of the black church have influenced British culture and worship today.
In Manchester, key figures from soul, pop and gospel gather to celebrate the unveiling of a new blue plaque in honour of a remarkable trailblazer, Sister Rosetta Tharpe. Pauline Black, lead singer of The Selecter, tells the story of how Sister Rosetta, known as the 'godmother of rock 'n' roll’, became one of the world’s most influential and pioneering Christian musicians. She explains how she brought church music from America to a wider audience, including in an iconic performance at a Manchester railway station in 1964.
Mark then meets Bazil and Leonn Meade of the world-renowned London Community Gospel Choir, who have been thrilling audiences for over 40 years. Mark explores the choir’s often controversial journey to performing with some of the world’s top artists, learning that faith has always been central to their music.
And there are brand new music recordings especially for the season. In the iconic New Testament Assembly Church in Tooting, the London Community Gospel Choir raise the praise with uplifting worship. And there are powerful solos from West End stars Sharlene Hector and Lawrence Rowe, and renowned soul singer Sarah Brown:

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc:
The roadshow visits Bangor Castle in County Down, Northern Ireland, where finds include an unnervingly lifelike grasshopper vase, chairs that may have been destined for the Titanic and rare Japanese woodblock prints.
Lisa Lloyd is fascinated by a book demonstrating the different needlepoint skills honed by a young girl in the 1800s, including miniature fold-out booties and tie-on pockets, while Susan Rumfitt is dazzled by a characterful gold dachshund brooch.
Will Farmer is delighted to find an art deco opalescent glass vase and dish, while Mark Smith is moved to discover postcards from World War I battlefields, hand painted by a teenage soldier who never returned.
Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet hears how a ceramic vase in the shape of a giant grasshopper sat for decades in the front window at Grandma’s House in Dublin. Elsewhere, clocks and watches specialist Richard Price is stopped in his tracks by an impressive marble mantle clock that had lived on a bedroom floor.
Furniture specialist Lennox Cato sees a pair of skilfully crafted chairs produced for Belfast shipbuilders Harland and Wolff that may have been destined for the Titanic. Lee Young is impressed by a collection of 25 Japanese woodblock prints of Mount Fuji, bought in 1860 by the present owner’s great-grandfather.
Fiona Bruce learns about the remarkable wartime achievements of one of the members of the family who once lived in the house, Commander Barry Bingham VC, while miscellaneous expert Marc Allum challenges Fiona to correctly identify the function of three mystery objects from his own personal collection. programme.title: Thank You Sir Kev
programme.desc:
Prince William leads the tributes to Sir Kevin Sinfield for his remarkable fundraising for the MND community after taking on seven incredible challenges over seven years. His Royal Highness, who joined Sinfield on this year’s challenge, has said he is in awe of him and praises his quiet leadership, stating the rugby league legend is ‘a kind caring human being, but he’s still a lunatic’.
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours. In total, he has raised more than £13 million.
This touching documentary, made by BBC Breakfast, reflects on what has driven 'Sir Kev'. His parents, Ray and Beryl, talk about his upbringing and introduction to sport.
Former England rugby union captain Lewis Moody and ex-Premier League footballer Marcus Stewart talk about the difference he has made. Moody reveals Sinfield was one of the first people he spoke to when he was diagnosed with MND, while Stewart tells how Kevin rallied a whole community behind him.
Rob Burrow’s wife Lindsey reminds viewers that everyone needs a friend like Kev, while their daughter Macy says Sinfield is a real-life superhero. Rob’s mum, Irene, who first met Sinfield as a teenager, said she had called him ‘Sir Kev’ for many years.
As well as major sporting names, the documentary also features some of those living with MND and reveals how he has changed awareness. More than 5,000 people are living with the disease in the UK at any one time, and many of them and their families have supported Sinfield’s challenges. Some have joined Sir Kevin for a short distance as a way of showing support. Reporter - Sally Nugent Editor - Ben Kay-Coles Producer - Claire Ryan Production Manager - Laura Perrins.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.sub-title: Can dog deworming tablets cure cancer ║ S1E6/6
programme.desc:

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
While the teams get into the rhythm of their shopping, host Danny Sebastian indulges one of his passions at an exhibition in London. The Music Is Black: A British Story celebrates 125 years of the influence of black music on culture and communities. At the V&A East Museum, Danny tours the exhibition with curator Jacqueline Springer, looking at a vinyl record with the words ‘Race Records’ on the sleeve, a label designed to segregate black music from white artists. There’s a piano belonging to the first black artist to have a UK number one single, Winifred Attwell, engraved with the names of her fans, a dress worn by Dame Shirley Bassey at the 2013 Academy Awards and a Banksy-designed vest worn by Stormzy at Glastonbury in 2019.
Hoping to turn their items into auction hits are dad and daughter Erike and Melissa, and mum and daughter Angela and Katie. With hundreds of stalls to choose from, the teams go in search of profitable antiques with their experts, Irita Marriott and Jonathan Pratt.
While the red team sizes up a vintage measuring tape, the blues check out a crackle-glazed pig sculpture. Then it’s off to auction in Bourne End, Buckinghamshire, to try to sell their buys to the highest bidders. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
Ex-con Joe Ruby is a volunteer at a local priory, tending to the grounds, seeking forgiveness and attempting to start a new life, all under the kind but watchful eye of Father David.
But when the body of one of the monks is found hastily buried in a remote part of the priory grounds, Oxford-educated DI Rose O’Connell and her green second in command, DS Raj Singh, are sent to investigate.
The mysterious circumstances make it a tricky case to solve. What secrets are these sacred grounds hiding? And what do these God-fearing suspects know about the murder? There’s Brother Christopher, the gentle monk who loves to garden, Sister Marie, the stern but kindly nun who runs Bible class and Father David, the cryptic, ever-wise prior. Alongside them is the victim’s brother Benedict, who is someone in need of support and money. And then there’s Joe himself, who with his criminal past becomes suspect number one for Rose and Raj.
But when Joe comes up with some insights from his own dodgy history, Rose senses that he may prove useful after all.
Finding themselves investigating alongside each other, Joe and Rose set out to solve the mystery of who killed Brother Mark, frustrating each other at every turn, only to uncover a truth far more shocking than either anticipated. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
As part of the BBC’s Music Is Black season, renowned choir director Mark De-Lisser visits the new exhibition of the same name at the V&A East Museum and introduces exhilarating new music from the London Community Gospel Choir and special guests.
Mark takes a guided tour with curator Jacqueline Springer to explore how black music and the sounds and songs of the black church have influenced British culture and worship today.
In Manchester, key figures from soul, pop and gospel gather to celebrate the unveiling of a new blue plaque in honour of a remarkable trailblazer, Sister Rosetta Tharpe. Pauline Black, lead singer of The Selecter, tells the story of how Sister Rosetta, known as the 'godmother of rock 'n' roll’, became one of the world’s most influential and pioneering Christian musicians. She explains how she brought church music from America to a wider audience, including in an iconic performance at a Manchester railway station in 1964.
Mark then meets Bazil and Leonn Meade of the world-renowned London Community Gospel Choir, who have been thrilling audiences for over 40 years. Mark explores the choir’s often controversial journey to performing with some of the world’s top artists, learning that faith has always been central to their music.
And there are brand new music recordings especially for the season. In the iconic New Testament Assembly Church in Tooting, the London Community Gospel Choir raise the praise with uplifting worship. And there are powerful solos from West End stars Sharlene Hector and Lawrence Rowe, and renowned soul singer Sarah Brown:

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc:
The roadshow visits Bangor Castle in County Down, Northern Ireland, where finds include an unnervingly lifelike grasshopper vase, chairs that may have been destined for the Titanic and rare Japanese woodblock prints.
Lisa Lloyd is fascinated by a book demonstrating the different needlepoint skills honed by a young girl in the 1800s, including miniature fold-out booties and tie-on pockets, while Susan Rumfitt is dazzled by a characterful gold dachshund brooch.
Will Farmer is delighted to find an art deco opalescent glass vase and dish, while Mark Smith is moved to discover postcards from World War I battlefields, hand painted by a teenage soldier who never returned.
Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet hears how a ceramic vase in the shape of a giant grasshopper sat for decades in the front window at Grandma’s House in Dublin. Elsewhere, clocks and watches specialist Richard Price is stopped in his tracks by an impressive marble mantle clock that had lived on a bedroom floor.
Furniture specialist Lennox Cato sees a pair of skilfully crafted chairs produced for Belfast shipbuilders Harland and Wolff that may have been destined for the Titanic. Lee Young is impressed by a collection of 25 Japanese woodblock prints of Mount Fuji, bought in 1860 by the present owner’s great-grandfather.
Fiona Bruce learns about the remarkable wartime achievements of one of the members of the family who once lived in the house, Commander Barry Bingham VC, while miscellaneous expert Marc Allum challenges Fiona to correctly identify the function of three mystery objects from his own personal collection. programme.title: Desmond Armstrong: America's World Cup Pioneer
programme.desc:
Desmond Armstrong was the first US-born black player to represent the United States men's national football team at a World Cup. He was part of the squad that did the unthinkable: qualifying for Italia 90 at a time when the US had no professional league and football wasn't taken seriously.

programme.title: Thank You Sir Kev
programme.desc:
Prince William leads the tributes to Sir Kevin Sinfield for his remarkable fundraising for the MND community after taking on seven incredible challenges over seven years. His Royal Highness, who joined Sinfield on this year’s challenge, has said he is in awe of him and praises his quiet leadership, stating the rugby league legend is ‘a kind caring human being, but he’s still a lunatic’.
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours. In total, he has raised more than £13 million.
This touching documentary, made by BBC Breakfast, reflects on what has driven 'Sir Kev'. His parents, Ray and Beryl, talk about his upbringing and introduction to sport.
Former England rugby union captain Lewis Moody and ex-Premier League footballer Marcus Stewart talk about the difference he has made. Moody reveals Sinfield was one of the first people he spoke to when he was diagnosed with MND, while Stewart tells how Kevin rallied a whole community behind him.
Rob Burrow’s wife Lindsey reminds viewers that everyone needs a friend like Kev, while their daughter Macy says Sinfield is a real-life superhero. Rob’s mum, Irene, who first met Sinfield as a teenager, said she had called him ‘Sir Kev’ for many years.
As well as major sporting names, the documentary also features some of those living with MND and reveals how he has changed awareness. More than 5,000 people are living with the disease in the UK at any one time, and many of them and their families have supported Sinfield’s challenges. Some have joined Sir Kevin for a short distance as a way of showing support. Reporter - Sally Nugent Editor - Ben Kay-Coles Producer - Claire Ryan Production Manager - Laura Perrins.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.sub-title: Can dog deworming tablets cure cancer ║ S1E6/6
programme.desc:
Stacey looks into an emotive and controversial trend claiming that over-the-counter dog deworming tablets fenbendazole can cure cancer. She meets Mel, a woman from Kent with stage four cancer, who decided to start the DIY treatment and chart her progress on her socials.
Further sleuthing takes Stacey to America to meet Joe Tippens, the originator of the trend, whose claims sparked nationwide panic buying of fenbendazole in South Korea. That leads Stacey to explore why medical trials have never been fully funded, and to ask Dr Alex and Dr Nighat about the potential side-effects and the benefits of sticking to NHS-approved treatments. programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: The Celebrity Inner Circle
programme.desc:
Amanda Holden hosts this exciting quiz show, packed with strategy, high stakes and lots of surprises.
Five contestants choose a celebrity partner and are assigned a secret stash of cash, worth anything from zero to a whopping £6,000.
The twist? Each pair only knows their own value before being thrown into a battle of wits, nerve and strategic gameplay across a series of challenging rounds.
Their mission? Uncover who has got what amount, outsmart their rivals and secure their spot in the final. Each round brings tense showdowns, with the winning pair earning immunity and a game-changing power, before the group votes to cast a contestant and their celebrity partner out of the game.
Only two contestants will make it to the cash builder and the chance to double their combined cash before the dramatic final, where they must make the ultimate decision. Will they choose to split their combined prize money equally, or will one player attempt to take it all, leaving the other with nothing? In this show, it’s not just about what you know. It’s about who you can trust.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
Ex-con Joe Ruby is a volunteer at a local priory, tending to the grounds, seeking forgiveness and attempting to start a new life, all under the kind but watchful eye of Father David.
But when the body of one of the monks is found hastily buried in a remote part of the priory grounds, Oxford-educated DI Rose O’Connell and her green second in command, DS Raj Singh, are sent to investigate.
The mysterious circumstances make it a tricky case to solve. What secrets are these sacred grounds hiding? And what do these God-fearing suspects know about the murder? There’s Brother Christopher, the gentle monk who loves to garden, Sister Marie, the stern but kindly nun who runs Bible class and Father David, the cryptic, ever-wise prior. Alongside them is the victim’s brother Benedict, who is someone in need of support and money. And then there’s Joe himself, who with his criminal past becomes suspect number one for Rose and Raj.
But when Joe comes up with some insights from his own dodgy history, Rose senses that he may prove useful after all.
Finding themselves investigating alongside each other, Joe and Rose set out to solve the mystery of who killed Brother Mark, frustrating each other at every turn, only to uncover a truth far more shocking than either anticipated. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
As part of the BBC’s Music Is Black season, renowned choir director Mark De-Lisser visits the new exhibition of the same name at the V&A East Museum and introduces exhilarating new music from the London Community Gospel Choir and special guests.
Mark takes a guided tour with curator Jacqueline Springer to explore how black music and the sounds and songs of the black church have influenced British culture and worship today.
In Manchester, key figures from soul, pop and gospel gather to celebrate the unveiling of a new blue plaque in honour of a remarkable trailblazer, Sister Rosetta Tharpe. Pauline Black, lead singer of The Selecter, tells the story of how Sister Rosetta, known as the 'godmother of rock 'n' roll’, became one of the world’s most influential and pioneering Christian musicians. She explains how she brought church music from America to a wider audience, including in an iconic performance at a Manchester railway station in 1964.
Mark then meets Bazil and Leonn Meade of the world-renowned London Community Gospel Choir, who have been thrilling audiences for over 40 years. Mark explores the choir’s often controversial journey to performing with some of the world’s top artists, learning that faith has always been central to their music.
And there are brand new music recordings especially for the season. In the iconic New Testament Assembly Church in Tooting, the London Community Gospel Choir raise the praise with uplifting worship. And there are powerful solos from West End stars Sharlene Hector and Lawrence Rowe, and renowned soul singer Sarah Brown:

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc:
The roadshow visits Bangor Castle in County Down, Northern Ireland, where finds include an unnervingly lifelike grasshopper vase, chairs that may have been destined for the Titanic and rare Japanese woodblock prints.
Lisa Lloyd is fascinated by a book demonstrating the different needlepoint skills honed by a young girl in the 1800s, including miniature fold-out booties and tie-on pockets, while Susan Rumfitt is dazzled by a characterful gold dachshund brooch.
Will Farmer is delighted to find an art deco opalescent glass vase and dish, while Mark Smith is moved to discover postcards from World War I battlefields, hand painted by a teenage soldier who never returned.
Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet hears how a ceramic vase in the shape of a giant grasshopper sat for decades in the front window at Grandma’s House in Dublin. Elsewhere, clocks and watches specialist Richard Price is stopped in his tracks by an impressive marble mantle clock that had lived on a bedroom floor.
Furniture specialist Lennox Cato sees a pair of skilfully crafted chairs produced for Belfast shipbuilders Harland and Wolff that may have been destined for the Titanic. Lee Young is impressed by a collection of 25 Japanese woodblock prints of Mount Fuji, bought in 1860 by the present owner’s great-grandfather.
Fiona Bruce learns about the remarkable wartime achievements of one of the members of the family who once lived in the house, Commander Barry Bingham VC, while miscellaneous expert Marc Allum challenges Fiona to correctly identify the function of three mystery objects from his own personal collection. programme.title: Desmond Armstrong: America's World Cup Pioneer
programme.desc:
Desmond Armstrong was the first US-born black player to represent the United States men's national football team at a World Cup. He was part of the squad that did the unthinkable: qualifying for Italia 90 at a time when the US had no professional league and football wasn't taken seriously.
This documentary explores how he got there, the racial tensions of that era and his work as a youth academy coach in Antioch, Nashville, making the sport accessible to immigrant communities against a backdrop of heightened immigration enforcement. programme.title: Thank You Sir Kev
programme.desc:
Prince William leads the tributes to Sir Kevin Sinfield for his remarkable fundraising for the MND community after taking on seven incredible challenges over seven years. His Royal Highness, who joined Sinfield on this year’s challenge, has said he is in awe of him and praises his quiet leadership, stating the rugby league legend is ‘a kind caring human being, but he’s still a lunatic’.
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours. In total, he has raised more than £13 million.
This touching documentary, made by BBC Breakfast, reflects on what has driven 'Sir Kev'. His parents, Ray and Beryl, talk about his upbringing and introduction to sport.
Former England rugby union captain Lewis Moody and ex-Premier League footballer Marcus Stewart talk about the difference he has made. Moody reveals Sinfield was one of the first people he spoke to when he was diagnosed with MND, while Stewart tells how Kevin rallied a whole community behind him.
Rob Burrow’s wife Lindsey reminds viewers that everyone needs a friend like Kev, while their daughter Macy says Sinfield is a real-life superhero. Rob’s mum, Irene, who first met Sinfield as a teenager, said she had called him ‘Sir Kev’ for many years.
As well as major sporting names, the documentary also features some of those living with MND and reveals how he has changed awareness. More than 5,000 people are living with the disease in the UK at any one time, and many of them and their families have supported Sinfield’s challenges. Some have joined Sir Kevin for a short distance as a way of showing support. Reporter - Sally Nugent Editor - Ben Kay-Coles Producer - Claire Ryan Production Manager - Laura Perrins.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. The Music Is Black: A British Story celebrates 125 years of the influence of black music on culture and communities. At the V&A East Museum, Danny tours the exhibition with curator Jacqueline Springer, looking at a vinyl record with the words ‘Race Records’ on the sleeve, a label designed to segregate black music from white artists. There’s a piano belonging to the first black artist to have a UK number one single, Winifred Attwell, engraved with the names of her fans, a dress worn by Dame Shirley Bassey at the 2013 Academy Awards and a Banksy-designed vest worn by Stormzy at Glastonbury in 2019.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
Ex-con Joe Ruby is a volunteer at a local priory, tending to the grounds, seeking forgiveness and attempting to start a new life, all under the kind but watchful eye of Father David.
But when the body of one of the monks is found hastily buried in a remote part of the priory grounds, Oxford-educated DI Rose O’Connell and her green second in command, DS Raj Singh, are sent to investigate.
The mysterious circumstances make it a tricky case to solve. What secrets are these sacred grounds hiding? And what do these God-fearing suspects know about the murder? There’s Brother Christopher, the gentle monk who loves to garden, Sister Marie, the stern but kindly nun who runs Bible class and Father David, the cryptic, ever-wise prior. Alongside them is the victim’s brother Benedict, who is someone in need of support and money. And then there’s Joe himself, who with his criminal past becomes suspect number one for Rose and Raj.
But when Joe comes up with some insights from his own dodgy history, Rose senses that he may prove useful after all.
Finding themselves investigating alongside each other, Joe and Rose set out to solve the mystery of who killed Brother Mark, frustrating each other at every turn, only to uncover a truth far more shocking than either anticipated. Next to try to make a sale is toy collector Rob, who brings a smile to everyone’s face with his novelty horror-themed coin bank. Valuation expert Simon confesses to owning one in his younger days, but will nostalgia alone be enough to convince him to join the bidding?
As if that’s not enough excitement, Peter has a rare treat for all the antique lovers - a smoking Turk automaton. But our buyers will have to dig deep if they want to take this treasure home. Oh, and any resemblance to the Rag & Bone Bros is entirely coincidental.
Number four through the doors of Leith Theatre is well-travelled Billie. She’s keen to find out if anyone will bend over backwards to bid on her folding Indian chair.
Lastly, it’s brains versus brawn as one of Scotland’s strongest men faces off against the wily dealers. But Callum has brought a secret weapon - his six-year-old daughter Georgia. Will her promise of a guinea pig for everyone if they shift dad’s atlas stone be enough to make Jo and the rest roll over? One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies.
They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
As part of the BBC’s Music Is Black season, renowned choir director Mark De-Lisser visits the new exhibition of the same name at the V&A East Museum and introduces exhilarating new music from the London Community Gospel Choir and special guests.
Mark takes a guided tour with curator Jacqueline Springer to explore how black music and the sounds and songs of the black church have influenced British culture and worship today.
In Manchester, key figures from soul, pop and gospel gather to celebrate the unveiling of a new blue plaque in honour of a remarkable trailblazer, Sister Rosetta Tharpe. Pauline Black, lead singer of The Selecter, tells the story of how Sister Rosetta, known as the 'godmother of rock 'n' roll’, became one of the world’s most influential and pioneering Christian musicians. She explains how she brought church music from America to a wider audience, including in an iconic performance at a Manchester railway station in 1964.
Mark then meets Bazil and Leonn Meade of the world-renowned London Community Gospel Choir, who have been thrilling audiences for over 40 years. Mark explores the choir’s often controversial journey to performing with some of the world’s top artists, learning that faith has always been central to their music.
And there are brand new music recordings especially for the season. In the iconic New Testament Assembly Church in Tooting, the London Community Gospel Choir raise the praise with uplifting worship. And there are powerful solos from West End stars Sharlene Hector and Lawrence Rowe, and renowned soul singer Sarah Brown:

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc:
The roadshow visits Bangor Castle in County Down, Northern Ireland, where finds include an unnervingly lifelike grasshopper vase, chairs that may have been destined for the Titanic and rare Japanese woodblock prints.
Lisa Lloyd is fascinated by a book demonstrating the different needlepoint skills honed by a young girl in the 1800s, including miniature fold-out booties and tie-on pockets, while Susan Rumfitt is dazzled by a characterful gold dachshund brooch.
Will Farmer is delighted to find an art deco opalescent glass vase and dish, while Mark Smith is moved to discover postcards from World War I battlefields, hand painted by a teenage soldier who never returned.
Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet hears how a ceramic vase in the shape of a giant grasshopper sat for decades in the front window at Grandma’s House in Dublin. Elsewhere, clocks and watches specialist Richard Price is stopped in his tracks by an impressive marble mantle clock that had lived on a bedroom floor.
Furniture specialist Lennox Cato sees a pair of skilfully crafted chairs produced for Belfast shipbuilders Harland and Wolff that may have been destined for the Titanic. Lee Young is impressed by a collection of 25 Japanese woodblock prints of Mount Fuji, bought in 1860 by the present owner’s great-grandfather.
Fiona Bruce learns about the remarkable wartime achievements of one of the members of the family who once lived in the house, Commander Barry Bingham VC, while miscellaneous expert Marc Allum challenges Fiona to correctly identify the function of three mystery objects from his own personal collection. Presenter - Fiona Bruce Production Manager - Ash Morris Series Editor - Robert Murphy Series Producer - Rae Gilder Cooke.

programme.title: Desmond Armstrong: America's World Cup Pioneer
programme.desc:
Desmond Armstrong was the first US-born black player to represent the United States men's national football team at a World Cup. He was part of the squad that did the unthinkable: qualifying for Italia 90 at a time when the US had no professional league and football wasn't taken seriously.
This documentary explores how he got there, the racial tensions of that era and his work as a youth academy coach in Antioch, Nashville, making the sport accessible to immigrant communities against a backdrop of heightened immigration enforcement. programme.title: Thank You Sir Kev
programme.desc:
Prince William leads the tributes to Sir Kevin Sinfield for his remarkable fundraising for the MND community after taking on seven incredible challenges over seven years. His Royal Highness, who joined Sinfield on this year’s challenge, has said he is in awe of him and praises his quiet leadership, stating the rugby league legend is ‘a kind caring human being, but he’s still a lunatic’.
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours. In total, he has raised more than £13 million.
This touching documentary, made by BBC Breakfast, reflects on what has driven 'Sir Kev'. His parents, Ray and Beryl, talk about his upbringing and introduction to sport.
Former England rugby union captain Lewis Moody and ex-Premier League footballer Marcus Stewart talk about the difference he has made. Moody reveals Sinfield was one of the first people he spoke to when he was diagnosed with MND, while Stewart tells how Kevin rallied a whole community behind him.
Rob Burrow’s wife Lindsey reminds viewers that everyone needs a friend like Kev, while their daughter Macy says Sinfield is a real-life superhero. Rob’s mum, Irene, who first met Sinfield as a teenager, said she had called him ‘Sir Kev’ for many years.
As well as major sporting names, the documentary also features some of those living with MND and reveals how he has changed awareness. More than 5,000 people are living with the disease in the UK at any one time, and many of them and their families have supported Sinfield’s challenges. Some have joined Sir Kevin for a short distance as a way of showing support. Reporter - Sally Nugent Editor - Ben Kay-Coles Producer - Claire Ryan Production Manager - Laura Perrins.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
On the final leg of his Midlands tour, Michael Portillo travels to Solihull, the home of iconic British brand Land Rover. He discovers that their factory, now owned by Indian Tata Motors, produced the first Land Rover model in the 1940s. Michael gets to put a modern Range Rover through its paces in a hair-raising off-road experience.
Just south of the city, in Hall Green, he visits the childhood neighbourhood of legendary author JRR Tolkien. He learns how the peaceful rural setting of Sarehole Mill provided inspiration for the fantasy world of Middle Earth in The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.
Michael finishes his tour at Britain’s first electric-only freight train operator, based at Birmingham International Station. He’s surprised to see how passenger trains that were new when he was minister for transport in the 1980s are now being used to carry parcels from Birmingham to Scotland. programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc:
Debut feature documentary from filmmaker and artist Myrid Carten, which unfolds as a powerful exploration of family, addiction and unconditional love. Carten turns her camera on her mother Nuala - who has both bipolar disorder and alcoholism – and her wider family, uncovering years of grief, conflict and resilience.
Blending intimate contemporary footage with childhood home videos and elements of her artistic practice, the film moves between humour and heartbreak as it explores the complexities of caring for someone living with mental illness and addiction. Emotionally raw, this film offers not only a unique first-person portrait of a family in crisis, but a universal reflection on how we can remain connected to those we love without losing ourselves.

Winehouse had a strong relationship with many parts of the BBC from when she launched herself as an artist back in 2004. In her short musical career, the north London native changed the landscape of modern pop culture, won countless awards, achieved critical acclaim and garnered global success before tragically dying at the tender age of 27.
Originally broadcast on the eve of the release of Asif Kapadia's Amy documentary film which explores Winehouse's life and death, here is an exploration of her music and her influences in her own words.
Consisting of performances and interviews entirely from the BBC archives, this film celebrates Amy's music, her influences, her challenges as an artist and her eternal brutal honesty in her own words. Featuring exclusive unseen and rarely seen songs from her triple platinum selling album Frank and revered Grammy-winning album Back to Black, the programme pays homage to the tattooed rebellious rock 'n' roll-spirited songstress who wrote smart, sad, soulful and original pop songs that became instant classics and inspired a generation. Katya Adler travels to Romania, Kosovo and Serbia. In Romania, Katya visits what will soon be Nato’s largest base in Europe. With Russia’s increasing aggression, Nato’s role in eastern Europe has been beefed up, and Romania has become strategically significant.
Katya’s next stop is Europe’s youngest country, Kosovo. She travels down Tony Blair Street – named after the UK prime minister who led the Nato mission there. Twenty-five years after the war ended, Katya meets the ethnic Serbs who still live in Kosovo – and insist the country is still Serbian.
Lastly, in Serbia, she visits a coal power plant and discovers there’s a battle for power taking place, with the west, Russia and China all wanting Serbia to be in their sphere of influence. For decades, the west has ignored this corner of Europe, but now, with so many other parts of the world gaining power and influence, the fear is Europe might be losing its foothold in this increasingly important region. programme.title: The Misadventures of Romesh Ranganathan
programme.desc:
As with most Brits, the headlines that flash into Romesh’s mind when he thinks about Romania are those around communism, the 90s orphan crisis, maligned Roma and its greatest celebrity export, Count Dracula. But is this image justified? Or does Romania have more to offer?
Landing in Bucharest, the only place in the country he’s heard of, Romesh meets political activist and media expert Angi Serban at the parliament palace, the astonishing architectural behemoth built on the command of the communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
Failing to warn him about the miles they’re about to clock, Angi takes Rom out of the capital to explore many amazing things that are overlooked in this vast slice of eastern Europe.
Romesh and Angi embark on a journey through the country’s seemingly endless and varied landscapes. Along the way, they sample Romania’s ghoulish side, seeing Transylvania and Vlad the Impaler’s castle, and paying their respects in a 'merry' cemetery. They also witness cars rolling up hills, drive along the spectacular yet dangerous Transfagarasan Highway, dance to world-famous Roma music and take part in a spiritual ceremony in Romania’s traditional heartland.
But whilst Romesh realises the beauty of Romania, he also learns how the hangover of the communist regime remains, what challenges are still faced today and why more people visiting would help the country to continue to move forward. programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc:
Journey across the tropical island of Madagascar and explore the unique and incredible wildlife it has to offer - from its famed lemurs to chameleons.
As the oldest island on earth, life has had time to evolve, and there are now more unique plants and animals on Madagascar than any other island.
It was formed nearly 90 million years ago when a giant landmass split apart, and Madagascar was cast adrift from east Africa. Braving the 400-mile ocean crossing from Africa, the first castaways arrived on the arid west of the island, and were met with vast deserts.
Ring-tailed lemurs are the direct descendants of one of the very first mammals to arrive, and they are thriving despite the arid conditions. They spend up to eight hours a day foraging in the Spiny Forest. Their plant-based diet includes plants with caustic sap that would burn human skin.
When humans arrived on the west coast, they too faced the hostile desert, high temperatures and droughts that can last a year. In the village of Ampotaka, the people have learnt to use baobab trees to help them survive. The trees grow up to 30 metres high and store vast quantities of water in their trunks. By hollowing out the inside of the trunk, the people create huge water tanks storing thousands of litres of water, which they can use when times are tough.
Tiny labord’s chameleons are unique to Madagascar and have the shortest lifespan of any land vertebrate – living for just four months. They time their hatching with the start of the rainy season when the going is good, and then the race is on for them to grow, mate and lay eggs before the dry season comes round once again.
One of the most dramatic places in Madagascar is known as the Grand Tsingy – 500 square miles of sharp limestone pinnacles sheltering small pockets of forest. To survive here, Decken’s sifakas must climb these shards of rock, sharp enough to shred human skin, and leap 30 feet between them.
A series of even higher peaks forms a mountainous spine running down the middle of Madagascar. Just a few thousand years ago, human settlers from Asia brought the skills to turn the steep mountainsides into rice paddies.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc:
In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda.
But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime.
With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc:
In the heart of south east Asia lies the tropical island of Borneo. Twice the size of the British Isles, it is the third largest island on earth and home to possibly the greatest diversity of life of any island - from flying lizards sun bears to orangutans. Its huge variety of habitats, from bustling coral reefs and ancient jungles to towering mountains, has given rise to over 60,000 species of plants and animals - many found nowhere else on earth.
Borneo’s shoreline is fringed by a tangle of mangroves and flooded forests, home to an extraordinary creature – the proboscis monkey. Their unique pot bellies allow them to survive on the nutrient-poor leaves, but even so, they must continually search for the freshest shoots. This means the whole family must cross one of many rivers that cut through the forest – patrolled by giant crocodiles. It is a drama rarely seen.
The island of Borneo is surrounded by some of the richest coral reefs in the world – a single reef can support more species of coral than the entire Caribbean Sea! This remarkable abundance attracted seafaring nomads, the Bajau Laut, ‘people of the sea’. Over generations their bodies have transformed, making them the ultimate human divers – but they are having to adapt to the modern world – using ingenuity to turn plastic waste that washes up on the beach to their advantage.
Heading inland are ancient forests, home to giants – the dipterocarps. Towering up to 100 metres high, they are the tallest rainforest trees in the world. A single tree can hold a thousand different species, and this intense competition has driven many animals to evolve in wondrous ways – on this island reptiles can fly.
At night, this competition in the jungle intensifies as many of Borneo’s 180 species of frog call for a mate. The bigger the frog, the louder the call: a problem for one of the smallest frogs on the island. In this never-before-filmed sequence, a male tree-hole frog, barely larger than a thumbnail, has come up with an ingenious solution to being heard above the noise.
Compared to the abundance of life in the treetops, the forest floor is an impoverished world. With little to eat, many of Borneo’s terrestrial mammals are smaller than on the mainland – including the exceedingly rare Bornean sun bear.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc:
Addenbrooke’s Hospital in Cambridge takes on some of the most challenging medical cases in the country. Its surgeons carry out operations that require such expertise that they are only performed here and in a handful of other UK centres.
One such procedure is a pelvic exenteration, so complicated it requires two surgeons to perform and two days to complete. The surgeons - colorectal consultant Nicola Fearnhead and consultant urologist Alex Colquhoun - only do around ten of these operations each year, where due to widespread cancer, all the organs in the pelvis need to be removed. It is such a massive, life-changing surgery that about 50 per cent of people who need the procedure for otherwise terminal illness, decide not to have it.
This time, their patient is 52-year-old Stuart, a father of two who has already had treatment for bowel cancer. However, the cancer has returned and the pelvic exenteration is his only chance for a cure. It will involve removing his rectum, bladder, prostate, surrounding lymph nodes as well as a large tumour on his kidney. The surgery is so radical it will leave him with no sexual function and needing two stomas; one for waste from his bowel and the other for urine.
On the first day of surgery, Nicola and Alex concentrate on taking out the disease. They must operate deep within Stuart’s pelvis to separate out the cancer and affected organs from the surrounding tissue and blood vessels. It is high-risk surgery because they need to operate near the body’s biggest blood vessels - the aorta and inferior vena cava - and the major vessels that branch off them. Damaging any of these could cause a major bleed.
But even if they manage to clear the disease, they still need a second day to reconstruct and create the two stomas. The most difficult one to create is for the urine produced by Stuart’s kidneys. Because his bladder will be removed, the drainage tubes from the kidneys – called ureters – need to be rerouted. This involves attaching these fragile tubes to a section of harvested bowel that will act as an outlet tube, which then has to be threaded through the abdominal wall to the surface without any kinks or distortions.

programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc:
This is a journey across Hawaii’s varied islands, discovering how they were made and the incredible wildlife that thrives there.
Hawaii is the most remote island chain on earth, and its tropical shores are hard to reach. But for the hardy creatures that can make it here, like the waterfall-climbing fish, carnivorous caterpillar and Laysan albatross, a land of opportunity awaits. From newly formed lava fields to lush jungles and vibrant coral reefs, these diverse and beautiful islands have it all.
Packed with surprising stories, the hidden gems of this tropical paradise are uncovered using stunning photography. Dramatic footage of the humpback whale heat run – the biggest courtship battle in the world – and intimate views of the world’s oldest known bird feeding its chick are just some of the highlights of what Hawaii has to offer.
The islands are so isolated that it used to be that one new species arrived every 100,000 years, but the arrival of people has radically changed the face of Hawaii. Now it gains around 20 new species every year. The remarkable Jackson’s chameleon is one of the animals recently introduced. Showing off its voracious appetite, the programme reveals how it is eating its way through the native animals and contributing to wiping them out entirely.
But this is a place where people are looking to the future and attempting to bring wildlife back from the brink of extinction. White terns, once extinct on the main islands of Hawaii, have gone from a single pair to over 2,000 birds in the last 60 years. It is a huge challenge, but people are seeking progressive new ways to live alongside nature to allow Hawaii’s wildlife to continue to thrive. programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn is Alistair Waite, with a fragile cake topper from his parents’ wedding cake, which holds memories of a childhood spent growing up in the circus. The centrepiece of the miniature circus scene is a faithful reproduction of the big top, of which Alistair’s father was the tent manager and where his mother performed each night. Paper restorer Angelina Bakalarou takes on the delicate task of restoring this precious memento, preserving a unique piece of circus heritage and family love.
Next in comes former children’s TV presenter Jenny Hanley, who brings along a cherished toy of great historical and personal significance: a stuffed monkey named Alphonse. This cheeky primate helped Jenny’s grandmother, Lisa Sheridan, take a series of relaxed and intimate portraits of the royal family, most notably of the young Princesses Elizabeth and Margaret. It was Alphonse’s job to attract the subject’s attention to the camera, but now, threadbare and worn, he’s in no condition to turn heads, royal or otherwise. It’s down to Bear Ladies Julie and Amanda to weave their magic, and bring him back to peak condition.
Londoner Abdul and his daughter Hannah are next through the barn doors, with a challenging proposal for horologist Steve Fletcher and woodworker Will Kirk. Their beautiful but very broken regulator clock was the dearest possession of Abdul’s father, who had been gifted it by a much-loved friend. Passed down to Abdul on his father’s death, the clock sadly didn’t survive the passage from India, and it is now in a pitiful state, leaving Abdul racked with guilt. It takes all of Will and Steve’s skills – and the help of a new face in the barn, screen printer Alasdair MacKay – to get this precious heirloom back to its very best.
Finally, Maureen Armstrong from Bristol presents a battered helmet from the Second World War era for the close attention of Lucia Scalisi. The helmet belonged to Maureen’s much-missed grandmother Dot, who served as a volunteer nurse during the Blitz and wore the helmet on duty as she tended to the wounded during bombing raids on Portsmouth. Now flaking and rust-spattered, Lucia sets to work to ensure that its history – and Dot’s name – are preserved for future generations.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc:
In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda.
But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime.
With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
Michael Portillo’s exploration of Essex reaches Chelmsford. At a huge construction site on the outskirts of the city he discovers Beaulieu Park, the first railway station to be built on the Great Eastern Main Line for over 100 years. Michael learns how the station is designed to alleviate congestion in Chelmsford city centre.
At Chelmsford Cathedral, the headquarters of the diocese of Chelmsford, Michael meets the bishop of Chelmsford, the Rt Revd Dr Guli Francis-Dehqani. He discovers one of the largest and most diverse dioceses in England and hears Bishop Guli’s extraordinary personal story of escape from Iran after the Islamic revolution of 1979.
Michael continues his rail journey on the Great Eastern Main Line and visits the historic riverside town of Maldon, with its pretty Thames barges. Michael learns about a medieval battle and handles a rare Viking sword.
He finishes this leg of his Essex journey in the coastal village of Tollesbury, with its strong maritime heritage and marshy landscape, a haven for birds and wildlife.
